name: SECE
rationale: Synchronous Electric Charge Extraction (SECE) is highly efficient for piezo harvesting. It extracts the available charge from the transducer capacitance at each voltage peak using an inductor and a switch, transferring it to the output capacitor via a diode. This avoids the continuous diode drops of a full-bridge rectifier and allows the output voltage to be decoupled from the piezo's open-circuit voltage, which is essential for meeting both the 1.8V minimum and 3.6V maximum across all load conditions.

name: SSHI_FullBridge
rationale: Synchronous Switch Harvesting on Inductor (SSHI) flips the voltage on the piezo capacitance at the extrema, significantly increasing the energy extracted per cycle compared to a standard rectifier. By combining a full-bridge rectifier (for energy extraction) with a parallel inductor-switch loop (for voltage inversion), we can boost the available power for heavy loads (S2) and use a Zener clamp to protect the load from overvoltage (S3).

name: SECE_DualL
rationale: This is a dual-path SECE variant using two separate inductors for the positive and negative peaks. While it uses more components, it can potentially offer better tuning and reduced crosstalk between the two extraction phases, ensuring more stable voltage levels across a wider range of excitation strengths and load values.

name: SSHI_Hybrid_Sync
rationale: The previous SSHI_FullBridge failed on S2 (heavy load) due to ripple and slow settlement. This suggests a need for higher power delivery or lower voltage drops. This design keeps the SSHI inversion circuit and the full-bridge rectifier but adds a second SYNC controller to implement a partial synchronous return path. By replacing the return diodes (D3, D4) with switches (S2, S3) controlled by G2, we reduce the forward voltage drop from ~0.25V to nearly 0V. This increases the net current delivered to the output capacitor, which should reduce ripple (by providing more energy per cycle) and improve settlement time (by decreasing the equivalent charging resistance).

name: HalfBridge_SSHI
rationale: The previous best design (SSHI_FullBridge) failed on ripple and settling for the heavy load (S2), and potentially had a slow startup due to the two-diode drop of the full-bridge rectifier (approx 0.5V). This topology implements a Half-Bridge SSHI: one piezo terminal (pzn) is tied to ground, and the other (pzp) is flipped using an inductor L1 and switch S1 at every peak. The resulting positive voltage is rectified by a single diode D1, reducing the forward voltage drop to 0.25V. This should improve startup time (tup) and, combined with a larger output capacitor C1 (which the optimizer can now better utilize), reduce the ripple (vpp) and settling (dv) issues on S2.

name: Doubler_SSHI
rationale: The SSHI_FullBridge was very close to passing, failing only on ripple and settling time under heavy load (S2). This suggests a trade-off between Cout for ripple and Cout for settling speed. I'm replacing the full-bridge rectifier with a symmetric voltage-doubler (Greinacher) structure combined with SSHI. This changes the charging characteristics and may allow the optimizer to find a better balance between ripple and stability, while still benefiting from the energy boost of the L-S flipping circuit.

name: HalfBridge_SSHI_Symmetric
rationale: The SSHI_FullBridge was nearly successful but failed on S2 ripple and settling due to a conflict between storage capacitor size (ripple) and startup time (settling). The HalfBridge_SSHI settled at a lower voltage (2.14V in S2), which avoided these issues, but it slightly failed the minimum voltage and startup for S4 (1.78V vs 1.8V). By changing the flipping switch S1 from connecting to 0 (ground) to connecting to pzn (the other piezo terminal), we implement a more efficient SSHI flip, increasing the extracted energy. Combined with a half-bridge rectifier (D1, R1), we expect to maintain a lower steady-state voltage than the FullBridge (reducing ripple and dV) while increasing the power enough to pass S4.

name: DualPath_SECE
rationale: The previous best design, SSHI_FullBridge, failed on S2 (heavy load) due to ripple and settling time, suggesting a need for more efficient energy transfer and better voltage stabilization. I am proposing a Dual-Path Synchronous Electric Charge Extraction (SECE) circuit. Instead of a full-bridge rectifier with a shunt inductor, this topology uses two symmetric paths: one for the positive peak and one for the negative peak. Each path consists of a switch, an inductor, and a diode. A single SYNC controller drives both switches; at each peak, only the diode corresponding to the higher potential conducts, transferring the energy stored in the piezo capacitance into the storage capacitor. This approach can provide more controlled energy bursts and higher efficiency, potentially reducing the ripple on the heavy load S2 while maintaining the voltage clamp with a Zener diode for S3.
